summary.title: Incident Response Framework and Protocols at Heroku
summary.one_liner: Heroku's step-by-step incident response process, built around an Incident Commander role borrowed from the Incident Command System, shows how to coordinate, communicate and run post-incident follow-up during outages.
takeaways: Assign one Incident Commander (IC) who decides whether an incident is worth investigating and coordinates the response.
Open a dedicated chat room and designate a comms person to post early public status updates, even if preliminary.
Keep a concise, versioned situation report (sitrep) updated so responders and support staff share the same picture.
Classify severity from SEV0 (critical) to SEV4 (minor), and escalate to executive and crisis communication teams for high-severity incidents.
After resolution, undo temporary changes (such as silenced alerts) and follow up with a post-mortem that feeds remediation items.
summary.summary: The article describes Heroku's incident response framework, based on the Incident Command System used in disaster response. It walks through the steps of an incident: paging an Incident Commander, moving to a Slack room, updating the public status site, sending situation reports, assessing and mitigating the problem, coordinating responders, cleaning up afterward, and running post-incident follow-up. It also explains escalation to Salesforce's Critical Incident Center and executive bridge calls for the most severe incidents, and notes influences from Crew Resource Management. The page is a conceptual process description rather than a tutorial with code.
